 BTC IS BACK TO ITS 2021 PEAK 🔁
 Five years ago this week, Bitcoin hit ~$69K for the first time.
 Today, it's trading at… ~$69K.
 BTC slipped under its November 2021 peak (~$69,045) late last night, and it's been hovering right around that level all morning.
 Anyone who bought the very top of the last cycle is roughly back to break-even, five years later.
 It also leaves BTC ~45% below its all-time high of ~$126K from October 2025.
 Last Saturday, John (our crypto analyst) called $71-72K strong support and said he expected "a LOT of support" to show up there.
 By Thursday, he described the buying as "more of a shrug than a stampede."
 BTC slid through $71K last night, dropped under the 2021 peak around 10:50pm ET, and briefly hit ~$67.9K at 1am.
 Then leverage did the rest: 
 $1.64B in liquidations over 24 hours.
 88.7% of that came from longs (traders betting on prices going up).
 The biggest single hit was a $31.1M BTC long on Hyperliquid, wiped out at $72,250.
 (With each forced sale pushing the price lower and triggering the next one.)
 Here's the full five-year round trip: 
 Source: Yahoo Finance, CoinGecko 
 This morning's PPI report didn't change much: 
 PPI (the producer price index, which tracks wholesale inflation) rose 0.3% in October, a touch below the 0.4% economists expected.
 Core PPI (the same measure minus food and energy) came in right on forecast.
 BTC bounced ~$740, then slid straight back under $69K.
 Traders now see a 100% chance the Fed raises interest rates on Dec 9 (according to CME FedWatch, a tool that turns futures prices into rate odds).
 Which leaves Bitcoin sitting right on top of the level John has called "the floor all year"…

 BTC IS BACK TO ITS 2021 PEAK (P2) 🔁
 The floor John is referring to is the 200-week moving average.
 It's Bitcoin's average weekly closing price over roughly four years, and it sits at ~$68K right now.
 It smooths out the daily noise, so big, patient buyers tend to step in around it.
 BTC hugged it for ~10 weeks this summer, then ran from ~$62.8K in mid-August to ~$86.5K by early October.
 John's call in his PRO update last night: "I think the 200-week gets tested… and I don't think we go back to the July low" (just under $58K).
 He's nudged the odds of a trip back there up from ~5% to 10-15%.
 For that to happen, he says BTC would have to drop "like a stone straight through" $68K with no support at all.
 Tim Warren is a little less sure: 
 On Wednesday, Tim (a crypto technical analyst and host of the Tim Warren Show) said he was 90% sure the bottom was in.
 He also said he'd cut that to ~70% if BTC lost $71K, and to ~55% if we got below $68,500.
 Both have now happened (the second briefly, overnight), putting him close to a coin flip.
 The bigger problem is who's missing: 
 Spot Bitcoin ETFs have now had six straight days of outflows, totaling ~$1.72B.
 BlackRock's IBIT, the biggest of the bunch, has seen withdrawals 10 days in a row.
 These funds took in ~$1.2B the day BTC hit its record high, but now they're heading for the exit:
 Source: Farside Investors 
 Here’s what to watch from here: 
 $68K through the weekend: If the 200-week holds, John expects it to act as a floor again.
 ~$73.1K: The 200-day moving average (BTC's average over the last ~200 days), and the first level BTC needs to win back.
 $75.5K: The bottom of the range BTC held from late August until this week. Reclaim that, and the bulls are back in business.
 Until then, John says he doesn't "trust any bounce."
 The big question for the weekend: 
 Do buyers finally show up at $68K, or wait for lower prices?

 Bitcoin just fell below $73K and ETFs posted their worst week since June. Meanwhile, the New York Stock Exchange is building its 24/7 stock market on Avalanche.
